solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Somewhere in America Derek gets clued up

parts.note: Del is the usual short form of the name Derek
someone clued up is informed, or aware

explanation.surface: A man called Derek finally gets the information he needs, somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets' simply joins the two pieces. Del is the familiar short form of Derek, as in Del Boy of the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a US state on the east coast, so it is indeed a place in America.

clue.text: Dour old male knocked over wine

indicators.note: something knocked over is turned the other way round, so the old-male pair is read backwards

parts.note: rosé is a pink wine

explanation.surface: A grim old man has upset a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns OM round to MO before the wine is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a gloomy, sullen, humourless manner; they are close synonyms.

clue.text: Gale not so bad? Reduce operations

definitions.meaning: a gale that is easing off is wind that has dropped, read literally as two words
to scale back an activity gradually before stopping it

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a whimsical reading of the phrase as a blowing wind that has fallen; the question mark flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to bring a business or activity gradually to an end, cutting back its operations.

clue.text: Name of German unaffected by revolution

definitions.note: a common German male first name that reads the same both ways

indicators.note: a word unchanged when turned round reads the same in both directions

parts.note: a common German male first name that reads the same both ways

explanation.surface: A German man's name stays the same however things turn.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common German male first name, borne by Bismarck among others.

clue.text: Mocking one "Reagan" in charge

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
Ronald Reagan, US president, was known as Ron

explanation.surface: Someone sarcastically calling a person 'Reagan' as though they were running the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironic remarks say the opposite of what is meant, often to mock or tease.

clue.text: Female to behave insincerely in truth

parts.note: to act is to put on a pretence

explanation.surface: A woman putting on a false front where honesty is called for.
explanation.definitionFit: A fact is something true, a piece of reality as opposed to fiction.

clue.text: Boozer opening — nothing inside

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across the words boozer and opening

explanation.surface: A pub opens its doors but there is nothing inside.
explanation.walkthrough: A boozer is British slang for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero is the number meaning nothing at all, a synonym of nil or nought.

clue.text: Favoured travel abroad in break

parts.note: being in is being in favour, popular

indicators.note: abroad can mean all over the place, so the letters of travel are scattered

explanation.surface: A well-liked person goes overseas during a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a pause or break, as between acts of a play.

clue.text: A king in control? Not after 1066!

definitions.text: A king in control? Not after 1066!

indicators.note: in places the a-plus-king pair inside the control word

parts.note: to have hold over something is to have control of it
R (Rex) is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Asking whether a monarch stayed in power, and answering that 1066 ended it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: 1066 is the year of the Norman Conquest, when the last Anglo-Saxon king of England died at Hastings.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Godwinson was crowned in January 1066 and lost his throne and life that October.

clue.text: Old sailors had a meal — fancy!

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors
ate means had something to eat

explanation.surface: Veteran seamen enjoyed a dinner and exclaim how elaborate it was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like an exclamation but is the adjective meaning elaborate.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy and ornate both describe something highly decorated and elaborate.

clue.text: Junior's first monkey trick

indicators.note: the first letter of the word junior's is taken

parts.note: a monkey is an ape in loose everyday usage, a primate

explanation.surface: A youngster's first bit of monkey business.
explanation.definitionFit: A jape is a practical joke or prank, a playful trick.

clue.text: One to observe pupils very closely

definitions.text: One to observe pupils very closely

parts.words: One to observe pupils very closely
parts.note: pupils here are the dark centres of the eyes, examined by an eye-care professional, not schoolchildren

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a strict teacher watching schoolchildren; the pupils are in fact the openings of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-test specialist peers into a patient's eyes, including the pupils, at close range.

clue.text: No disorder, doctor insisted

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters of insisted are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician firmly demanded that there be no mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' reads as a noun in the surface but is a verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidiness is neatness, the state of having no mess or disorder.

clue.text: Fancy design that could make IQ leap up?

indicators.note: the letters of IQ leap up could be made into another word by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Wondering whether some decorative pattern might boost someone's intelligence score.
explanation.definitionFit: Appliqué is decorative needlework in which cut-out fabric shapes are sewn onto a base, an ornamental design.

clue.text: A fellow into cannabis lost strength

indicators.note: the a-plus-fellow pieces go into the cannabis word

parts.note: weed is slang for cannabis
Ken is a man's name, so any fellow

explanation.surface: A man who got into drugs found himself losing his vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: To have weakened is to have become less strong, to have lost power.

clue.text: Child has ache rising in part of the body

parts.note: a kid is a child

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the ache word is backwards

parts.note: a yen is a longing or ache

explanation.surface: A child complains of a pain coming up somewhere in the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The kidneys are a pair of organs in the abdomen, so one is a part of the body.

clue.text: Chump expected to keep quiet

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so the quiet letter goes within

parts.note: due means expected, as a train due at noon
P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quiet

explanation.surface: A fool is told he ought to keep his mouth shut.
explanation.definitionFit: A dupe is a gullible person who is easily fooled, much like a chump.

clue.text: Summary of archaeological activity is in French

parts.note: a dig is an archaeological excavation
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A report summing up an excavation, written partly in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A digest is a condensed compilation or summary of information.

clue.text: Models misshapen? Not often

indicators.note: misshapen means put out of shape, so the letters of models are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether catwalk models are ever out of shape, and answering rarely.
explanation.definitionFit: Seldom means rarely, on few occasions.

clue.text: Service revolving around a biblical man

indicators.note: the service word, once turned, goes around the letter a
revolving means turning round, so the service word is read backwards

parts.note: use is service, as in being of use

explanation.surface: A church service going round and round a figure from scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolving' turns USE into ESU, and 'around' puts that round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Esau, elder twin of Jacob in Genesis, is a man from the Bible.

clue.text: Fellow, unknown, from offshore island

parts.note: a man is a fellow
X is the classic algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A mysterious stranger arriving from an island off the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Manx is the adjective for things belonging to the Isle of Man, an island off the British coast.

clue.text: No good having strong drink in small cup

parts.note: gin is a strong spirit

explanation.surface: Warning that it is unwise to drink spirits from a little cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A noggin is a small mug or cup, or a small measure of drink.

clue.text: A servant working in restaurants

indicators.note: working here means operating or being worked over, so the letters of a servant are rearranged

explanation.surface: A waiter employed in eateries.
explanation.definitionFit: Tavernas are small Greek restaurants or cafés.

clue.text: Refuse to take notice of cakes brought around

indicators.note: brought around means turned the other way, so the cakes word is read backwards

parts.note: buns are small cakes

explanation.surface: Someone ignores the pastries offered to them.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub someone is to pointedly ignore or rebuff them.
